findings.title: Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException with V2 enabled via the ClientRemovedEvent listener
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override clients(), so the V1 ClientPermissions implementation was used and this call worked. Now clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The listener guard only checks Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), which is typically enabled together with V2, so deleting any client in a realm where the fine-grained admin authz features are active will throw an exception inside the provider-event listener, likely failing or corrupting the client-removal flow. setPermissionsEnabled (and the other inherited V1 methods that no longer have a working implementation) need a no-op/compat implementation, or the listener must skip the clients branch for V2.

findings.title: No migration for realms that already initialized the admin permissions client: new Clients resource and scopes are never created
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Any realm that enabled admin permissions before this change has a resource server containing only the Users resource type and only the Users scopes (manage, view, impersonate, map-roles, manage-group-membership). The new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) and the "Clients" all-resource will never be created for such realms. Consequences: creating a Clients scope permission will fail (getScope lookup fails or resource lookup in getOrCreateResource finds nothing and throws "Could not map resource object..."), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission can hit a null "Clients" resource (see separate NPE finding). A migration step (or extending init() to create missing scopes/resources for existing admin permission clients) is required.

findings.title: NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist in hasPermission(ClientModel, String)
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no per-client resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource explicitly returns null when the resource type is unknown or no resource with that name exists (which is exactly the situation for realms initialized before this change, or if the "Clients" resource was never created). findByResource(server, null) will then throw a NullPointerException (or store-dependent error), turning a permission check into a 500 instead of returning false. The null case must be handled before calling findByResource.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission leaks the "Clients" all-resource name and ignores all-clients grants
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resources found by type Clients and adds resource.getName() for each granted resource. The "Clients" all-resource itself has type Clients, so if the admin holds a scope permission on it (granted for all clients), the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set — a value that is not a client ID. Worse, the intended semantics of an all-clients grant (the caller should see every client) are not handled at all: callers filtering client lists by this set will get an empty/incorrect result even though the admin is allowed to act on all clients. The method should either translate an all-clients grant into the full client set or exclude the type-level resource from the iteration.

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange permission evaluation paths
findings.body: canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. This method is part of the ClientPermissions contract used by token-exchange admin/permission evaluation code that is not gated on the V2 feature flag; if any of those paths execute while V2 is enabled, the caller receives a 500 error instead of an authorization decision. Either the V2 implementation must provide a decision (e.g., delegate to the scope-based evaluation or deny), or all call sites must be verified to be unreachable under V2 — with the unreachable ones documented/tested. The same concern applies to the other thrown methods if any remaining code path (e.g., the registerListener cleanup path) invokes them.
